channel.title: River Bend Outdoors
channel.description: Outdoor stories, field notes, and practical guides from River Bend Outdoors.

item.title: How My Son Taught Me to Make an Acorn Whistle
item.description: A walk with my boys became an unexpected lesson in making an acorn-cap whistle—and in who gets to be the teacher.

item.title: Denison Pequotsepos: The Little Adventure That Was Severely Underestimated
item.description: Our family went to a free winter wildlife class in Mystic and found live-animal exhibits, hands-on learning, and more trails than we had time to explore.

item.title: I Don't Know Where River Bend Outdoors Is Going. But I Know Why I Started.
item.description: Why River Bend Outdoors gives me a reason to get outside, follow my curiosity, keep learning, and make time for what matters.

item.title: When Hunting Season Changes a Hike: Lyme's Closures and Sharing Connecticut's Woods Safely
item.description: Ten Lyme preserves are closing on weekdays for firearm deer season, while hiking and hunting can coexist at nearby Nehantic State Forest. Here's how to know the difference and stay safe.

item.title: What Do Those Colored Marks on Trees Mean? An East Lyme Trail Blaze Guide
item.description: Blue, red, white, or two colors together—East Lyme's trail markers tell more than one story. Here's how to read them without assuming every park follows the same rules.

item.title: Oswegatchie Hills: Trails, Ponds, and a Few Surprises
item.description: Beyond the ballfields, rocky trails lead toward Clark Pond—a quiet stretch of water with a surprising history tied to Niantic’s fishing fleet.

item.title: Darrow Pond: A Park Worth Watching
item.description: A quiet East Lyme pond, a protected piece of open space and a new trail grant that could make the place easier to explore.
